NYSE TRF is extending operating hours to 9:00 p.m. Sunday–8:00 p.m. Friday with a one-hour daily pause, requiring FIX spec and market-data changes plus certification; the December 6, 2026 production cutover is a hard deadline for connectivity and testing readiness.
summary: FINRA/NYSE TRF will extend operating hours effective December 6, 2026 to 9:00 p.m. ET Sunday through 8:00 p.m. ET Friday, with a one-hour pause 8:00–9:00 p.m. ET Monday–Thursday, aligning with approved CTA/UTP SIP hour extensions and FINRA Rule 6300 Series changes. Certification opened October 2, 2026; remaining industry tests are November 6 (Tape A/B symbols only, cancels/corrections available), November 20, and December 4, running 11:00 p.m. ET Friday to 12:00 p.m. ET Saturday. From November 8, 2026, all Tape A and Tape B test symbols are available for Production testing during the Overnight Session; NYSE TRF Pillar FIX and NYSE BQT client specs are referenced.

rationale: IEX is changing D-Peg order on-entry behavior during active CQI/QII signal periods, with a phased symbol rollout starting November 17, 2026. This is a protocol/order-type change requiring system updates for firms trading IEX equities.
summary: IEX Equities will extend CQI and QII protections to on-entry behavior for Discretionary Peg (D-Peg) orders effective November 17, 2026. When the selected indicator is active, incoming D-Peg orders (DAY, GTX, SYS, GTT) will post at the less aggressive of one MPV below the NBB (buys) or above the NBO (sells), or the limit price, and will not execute on entry in locked/crossed markets. Rollout: test symbols Nov 17, ten non-test symbols Nov 18, symbols V-Z Nov 19, all symbols Nov 20. Updated functionality is available in ITF.

summary: Nasdaq Texas filed conforming fee changes to align with Nasdaq's new consolidated feed products, Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus, which combine Depth-of-Book and Top-of-Book data from Nasdaq, Nasdaq Texas, and Nasdaq PSX equities. The filing waives Nasdaq Texas and PSX market data distributor fees for firms consolidating those feeds for external redistribution and adds Nasdaq Basic Plus to consolidation-fee provisions, supporting the 23x5 schedule set to begin December 2026.

rationale: This is a routine fee-conforming rule filing for Nasdaq PHLX market-data distributor fees tied to new Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus products; it is fee-focused rather than a protocol or connectivity change, though the new consolidated feed products and the December 2026 23x5 schedule are structurally notable.
summary: Nasdaq PHLX filed conforming rule changes to Equity 7, Section 3 to align PSX market-data distributor fees with Nasdaq's new Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus consolidated feed products. The filing waives PSX TotalView distributor fees for firms consolidating PSX TotalView with Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas TotalView for external redistribution, adds Nasdaq Basic Plus as a product subject to consolidation fees, and clarifies monthly administrative and data consolidation fees for firms receiving Nasdaq Last Sale Plus or Nasdaq Basic Plus. The consolidated feeds are designed to support the 23-hour, 5-day-per-week schedule set to begin in December 2026.

rationale: BOX is adopting rules to enable electronic auction trading of FLEX Equity Options, a new order/auction type on its electronic market, directly affecting options market-making infrastructure and protocol/order-type support.
summary: BOX filed to adopt rules governing FLEX Equity Options trading in electronic auctions, adding proposed Rules 7155 (FLEX PIP) and 7275 (FLEX Solicitation Auction) alongside existing Rule 7605 (FOO Orders) under Rule 5055. The proposal mirrors CBOE and Nasdaq ISE electronic FLEX models but omits CBOE's Electronic FLEX Auctions and percentage-based pricing, limiting BOX to price improvement and solicitation auctions. Filed as immediately effective.

rationale: IEX rule filing amending Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker resumption rules in connection with the industry-wide shift to 23/5 trading; structurally notable for market-wide halt handling but not a protocol or connectivity change.
summary: IEX proposes to amend Rule 11.271 so that after a Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker halt, trading resumes consistent with the upcoming 23/5 extended trading environment beginning December 6, 2026. IEX's own sessions remain 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. ET (Pre-Market, Regular, Post-Market), but the uniform Level 3 MWCB rules across all exchanges are being modified because some venues will offer overnight trading.

rationale: New consolidated Nasdaq equity data products (TotalView Plus, Basic Plus) replace three separate feeds with one, tied to the December 2026 overnight trading transition — a feed-product/connectivity change relevant to market-data infrastructure, though equity-only and not options.
summary: Nasdaq proposes fee schedules for two new consolidated data products: Nasdaq TotalView Plus (replacing Nasdaq TotalView, Nasdaq Texas TotalView, and PSX TotalView) and Nasdaq Basic Plus (replacing Nasdaq Basic, Nasdaq Texas BBO/Last Sale, and PSX BBO/Last Sale). The products consolidate three feeds into one to reduce market data, networking, and connectivity costs and support the 23-hour, 5-day schedule set to begin in December 2026. Fees are set at or below current combined underlying product fees.

Corresponding references throughout the rules are updated to contemplate multiple clearing agencies, with OCC separately defined for options it continues to issue and clear.

TOPS, DEEP, and Channelized DEEP+ are unaffected, and no additional fees apply.
